Scatter aggregation over groups

Source: R/aggregations.R
scatter.Rd

Reduce rows of src into dim_size groups given by index: row k of the result combines all rows j with index[j] == k. These are the aggregation kernels used by message_passing(); they are vectorized torch operations (index_add, scatter_reduce) and differentiable.

Usage

scatter_sum(src, index, dim_size)

scatter_count(index, dim_size, dtype = torch_float(), device = NULL)

scatter_mean(src, index, dim_size)

scatter_max(src, index, dim_size)

scatter_min(src, index, dim_size)

scatter_std(src, index, dim_size, eps = 1e-05)

scatter_softmax(src, index, dim_size)

scatter_aggregate(src, index, dim_size, aggr = "sum")

Arguments

src

Tensor with one row per element (for example per edge).

index

One based long tensor (or integer vector) of group ids, one per row of src.

dim_size

Number of groups (for example the number of nodes).

dtype, device

Dtype and device of the count tensor.

eps

Constant added under the square root in scatter_std().

aggr

One or more of "sum" (alias "add"), "mean", "max", "min", "std".

Value

A tensor with dim_size rows.

Details

  • scatter_sum(): sum of rows. Empty groups give 0.

  • scatter_mean(): sum divided by the group size. Empty groups give 0.

  • scatter_max(), scatter_min(): elementwise maximum or minimum. Empty groups give 0. Gradients flow to the selected entries; ties split the gradient as torch defines for scatter_reduce.

  • scatter_std(): population standard deviation, with a small constant inside the square root so the gradient stays finite.

  • scatter_softmax(): softmax of src within each group (used for attention over incoming edges); columns are treated separately.

  • scatter_aggregate(): dispatch by name; several names give their results concatenated column wise.

Examples

if (torch::torch_is_installed()) {
  src <- torch::torch_tensor(matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 4), 4, 1))
  idx <- torch::torch_tensor(c(1L, 1L, 2L, 2L), dtype = torch::torch_long())
  scatter_sum(src, idx, 3)
  scatter_mean(src, idx, 3)
  scatter_max(src, idx, 3)
}
#> torch_tensor
#>  2
#>  4
#>  0
#> [ CPUFloatType{3,1} ]
